question: To estimate the average work experience of MBA students at a management institute, five students are selected at random from each type of background, say commerce, science and engineering. This type of sampling is called:
solution:
The correct answer is **Stratified sampling. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stratified sampling** is a sampling technique where the population is divided into subgroups (strata) based on certain attributes

 
 
• and then a sample is taken from each stratum. In the given scenario
 
• the population of MBA students is divided into three strata based on their background (commerce, science and engineering)
 
• and then five students are selected at random from each stratum.
 
 
 
• This helps to ensure that the sample is representative of the population and reduces sampling bias. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stratified sampling** is often used when the population is heterogeneous and you want to ensure that each subgroup is adequately represented in the sample.
 
• This helps to minimize sampling error and improve the accuracy of the results.
 
• In general, the sample size for each stratum should be proportional to the size of the stratum in the population.
 
• In this way, each stratum has a fair chance of being selected, and the results are more representative of the population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__ **

 
• It's important to note that stratified sampling is not always the best choice
 
 
• as it can be time-consuming and costly to divide the population into strata and select a sample from each.
 
 
 
• Other factors, such as the nature of the research question and the availability of resources
 
• It should be considered when choosing the most appropriate sampling technique.
